summary: Gareth Sparham is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned a PhD under Ashok Aklujkar at the University of British Columbia, later holding posts there and at the University of Michigan.

Gary A. Tubb works in Indology and studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He has held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

Gary D. DeAngelis specializes in religious studies and philosophy. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi and William J. Johnson, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).
Gary Snyder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley, and held posts at UC Davis (~1986–2002) and UC Irvine (attested 2002).

Gary Urton works in history and archaeology. After studying at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1969–1979), he held posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).
Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1834. He later held posts at the University of Turin (~1852–1891) and as a librarian at the Royal Library of Turin (~1859–1891).
Gavin D'Costa specializes in religious studies. He studied at the University of Birmingham (~1980–1985) and became Professor in Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (~2004).

Gavin Flood is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He has held posts at Lampeter, the University of Stirling, the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and the University of Oxford.

Gelek is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He has served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and held visiting posts at the University of California and the University of Oxford.

Gembo Dorji specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and trained under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup, Dongyud Nyima, Jigme Choedra, and Sendrak Rinpoche.
Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1954 to 1964 and served as a professor at Kokugakuin University from ~1974 to 2005.
Genchi Kato specialized in religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899) and later held an academic post there (~1920–1934).

Gendun Chophel was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Labrang Monastery and Kumbum Monastery, where he studied under Sherab Gyatso (~1921–1927), and later held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Genjun Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under mentors including Tokuryu Yamauchi, he held professorships at Otani University, the University of Hamburg (1956), Harvard University, and a lectureship at Osaka University (attested 1995).
Genryu Kagamishima was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University (~1930–1935) and later served there as a professor from ~1949 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1948–1957) and held posts at Kokushikan University (~1964–1974) and Rissho University, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 2001.
Genzao was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Gyang mdzod Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. He studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University, later serving on the faculty at Uppsala (~1940–1973) and Stockholm University (attested 1990).

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University under Tsetan Chonjore and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003–2005).

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Virginia (~2006–2013) before joining Oregon State University as an assistant professor of religious studies (~2015).
